q7.answer: I never decided this. The document says the flag is the only source of current mode and the controller moves it, but not how workers learn of a change (poll, push or restart) or what happens to an invoice in flight at that moment. The only related mechanism is the charge key, which stops a repeat charge.

q8.answer: Gate evidence is the nightly comparison results, kept next to the shadow store (daily mismatch rate and invoice counts), plus a recorded Finance sign-off for gate B. The controller reads them and refuses a promotion whose gate is not met.

q9.answer: I did not name a component. I said only that the rollout starts automatically when the new engine's charge failure rate is above 2% over any 10-minute window in both or new_only before day 35, and that the rollback record is written when it starts. Which service measures the rate, and how, was not decided.

q10.answer: New charges are halted first. Due charges are delayed, not dropped, and are made in the ResumeOldCharging step. There the old engine charges every period that is due and has no recorded charge, after reconcile and, from new_only, after reprocessing skipped events.

q11.answer: The charge key (customer plus billing period) and the ledger. ReconcileCharges waits for in-flight charges to settle, then treats the ledger as the list of keys already charged. The old engine skips any key that already has a charge. I assumed the payment provider supports idempotency keys and flagged this as an open question.

q12.answer: The rollback moves to RollbackStuck and pages on-call. The mode is not yet old_only, the flag has not been flipped, and new charges stay halted, so due charges are delayed. On-call retries from the failed step, and every step is safe to re-run because it is keyed by charge key.
